bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5671796885422080 Project: open62541 Fuzzer: libFuzzer_open62541_fuzz_json_decode Fuzz target binary: fuzz_json_decode Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_open62541 Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash Address: Crash State: Variant_decodeJson UA_decodeJson fuzz_json_decode.cc Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 14620: In open62541's JSON decoder, searchObjectForKeyRec finds a matching key ("Type") at the last valid token and increments parseCtx->index past it to point to the value, but does not check whether the new index is within tokenCount. When the key is the final jsmn token, the returned resultIndex points to an uninitialized slot in the heap-allocated tokenArray. Variant_decodeJson then reads tokenArray[resultIndex].end, .start, and .type, consuming uninitialized heap memory. MSAN detects the use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.description: jsmn_parse consumes the attacker-controlled JSON input and produces the token array. For the PoC input {\"\"\"\"}'Type', jsmn produces tokenCount=4 and token[0].size=2 (counting key and value strings as individual children). This structure causes searchObjectForKeyRec to iterate beyond the object's structural boundary and match the stray 'Type' token.
source.value_from: jsmn_parse parses src->data (the PoC bytes) into parseCtx->tokenArray; vulnerability-relevant outputs: tokenCount=4, token[0].size=2, token[3]='Type'; value `parseCtx->tokenCount`; from `parseCtx->tokenCount = (UA_Int32)jsmn_parse(...)`

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Reads parseCtx->tokenArray[searchResultType].type where searchResultType=4 is one past the last valid token (tokenCount=4). The slot contains uninitialized heap data from the UA_malloc allocation. MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this line.

root_cause.description: After finding the key 'Type' at the last valid token (index=3), the code increments parseCtx->index to 4 without checking whether 4 < parseCtx->tokenCount. The out-of-bounds index 4 is then stored in *resultIndex and returned as a valid result. The fix adds a bounds check: if (parseCtx->index >= parseCtx->tokenCount) return UA_STATUSCODE_BADOUTOFRANGE.

tainted_value_origin.description: jsmn_parse produces tokenCount=4 and token[0].size=2 from the PoC input. The size=2 value causes searchObjectForKeyRec to iterate 2 times for the single key-value pair, reaching the stray 'Type' token at index 3. The tokenCount=4 makes index=4 out of bounds.

fine_trace.note: Allocates 1000 jsmntok_t slots (sizeof(jsmntok_t) * 1000) via UA_malloc. The allocation is not zeroed; slots beyond those filled by jsmn_parse contain uninitialized heap data. MSAN confirms: 'Uninitialized value was created by a heap allocation' at UA_memoryManager_malloc called from UA_decodeJson line 3303.

jsmn_parse parses the 12-byte PoC '{\"\"\"\"}'Type' and produces 4 tokens: token[0]={JSMN_OBJECT, start=0, end=6, size=2}, token[1]={JSMN_STRING, start=2, end=2}, token[2]={JSMN_STRING, start=4, end=4}, token[3]={JSMN_STRING, start=7, end=11 ('Type')}. Returns tokenCount=4. jsmn counts each child individually (key '' and value '' each increment size), so token[0].size=2 despite representing 1 key-value pair. Tokens 4..999 remain uninitialized.

Reads token[0].size=2 as objectCount. The loop 'for(i = 0; i < objectCount; i++)' will iterate twice, processing two 'key-value pairs'. But only one actual key-value pair exists ({'' : ''}); the second iteration reads token[3] ('Type') which is structurally outside the JSON object.

Second loop iteration (i=1): index=3 after first iteration consumed tokens 1 and 2. jsoneq compares token[3] (start=7, end=11, text='Type') against searchKey='Type'. Match succeeds (strlen match and strncmp match), entering the 'found' branch.

fine_trace.code:
parseCtx->index++; /*We give back a pointer to the value of the searched key!*/
*resultIndex = parseCtx->index;
fine_trace.note: Increments index from 3 to 4 to point to the presumed value token after the matched key. No bounds check: index=4 equals tokenCount=4, so it points one past the last valid token. Stores 4 in *resultIndex and returns UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD. The fix adds 'if (parseCtx->index >= parseCtx->tokenCount) return UA_STATUSCODE_BADOUTOFRANGE;' between the increment and the store.

Reads tokenArray[searchResultType].type where searchResultType=4. This slot was never written by jsmn_parse (only indices 0-3 are valid). The .type, .start, .end fields contain uninitialized heap data from the UA_malloc allocation. MSAN reports: 'use-of-uninitialized-value' at Variant_decodeJson line 2635. Line 2632 also reads the uninitialized .end and .start fields.

format.name: libFuzzer binary blob for fuzz_json_decode
format.contract: The 12-byte input {\"\"\"\"}'Type' is a malformed JSON object followed by a stray 'Type' string. jsmn tokenizes it into 4 tokens with the object having size=2 (two individual children). searchObjectForKeyRec iterates twice, matching 'Type' at the last token and returning an out-of-bounds index (4 == tokenCount) for the value. Variant_decodeJson then reads uninitialized heap memory at tokenArray[4].

parser_admitted.description: The PoC passes the tokenize call (jsmn_parse returns 4 > 0) and the top-level check (tokenCount >= 1 && tokenArray[0].type == JSMN_OBJECT), reaching the Variant_decodeJson dispatch at line 3328.

key_search_entered.description: lookAheadForKey(UA_JSONKEY_TYPE, ...) is called, which invokes searchObjectForKeyRec with depth=0. The search finds 'Type' in the second iteration and returns GOOD, so Variant_decodeJson proceeds to read the token at the returned index.
